narr: An active pattern in mid-September resulted in several reports of flash flooding in southern Utah, in addition to some isolated thunderstorm related wind gusts in northern Utah.
ev: Bureau of Land Management officials reported a flash flood wave moving down Phipps Wash toward the Escalante River. This is most likely associated with a brief thunderstorm which moved through the area between roughly 11:30 am MST to 12:30 pm MST and produced moderate to heavy rainfall. Event time is based upon report.

Park rangers relayed a report of flash flooding in Capitol Gorge, with floodwaters as much as 4 feet deep. This is associated with showers and thunderstorms which moved through the area between around 12:30 pm MST to 2:00 pm MST and produced around 0.50 inches of rainfall.

Moderate to heavy rain fell across Zion National Park and surrounding areas, with 3-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates of around 0.50 inches. As a result, the North Fork Virgin at Springdale river gauge recorded a rapid rise in stage from around 50 CFS to over 1200 CFS in under 2 hours. Additionally, park rangers at Zion National Park reported flooding in many slot canyons in the park, as well as several observed waterfalls.

Moderate to heavy rainfall from earlier in the day resulted in a flood wave traversing downstream along the Virgin River. The Virgin at Virgin river gauge recorded a flow increase from 333 CFS at 12:15 am MST to a peak of 2020 CFS at 2:00 am MST.
